column8: Tue 17 Nov: 3.0 store and questions only: one payment as 55.5 to 32.5 staff-months today (Keel arithmetic on verified pay); a yardstick, never a staffing plan or budget (case: no business plan for the residency); H9-119 and Q9-035 already carry a base, not the whole budget.

Tue 17 Nov: store only; the 9.1% cut is right (8j convention), but drop the analogy's which helps the half kept: 8q says a stronger NT$ comes with rising shares, not a larger half kept, and VT is never a Taiwan-dollar hedge.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; defines the staff-month (172.6 full-time hours, 2025) so a reader can check rows 1 and 22-25.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; the closer subsector (NT$42,997, 38.1 staff-months) tightens row 1's yardstick; performers, not residency managers.
Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (4) context at most: Taiwan's minimum wage rose eleven years running, +54.4% 2016-2027, 3.96% a year, read at source; past pace, never a forecast or a cost of Laura's residency.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (4) clause at most; never indexed by statute or inflation-linked by law: Art. 9 tells the committee to take the CPI's rise as its reference (參採) and the committee decides; Taiwan legal matters are out of the case's scope, so the law is context, never a requirement.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; one year's minutes (2026), so say in 2026 the committee agreed, never that the floor always rises by prices plus growth; row 8 carries the decade.
Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (4) store: the floor beat prices by about two points a year 2015-2026 except 2016 and 2021 (MOL's own words); 2026's CPI is a forecast, so label it.

Tue 17 Nov: never a Table 3 row: Table 3 is cut to one page of seven, and this watch has no action, sits after the payments are owned and tracks running costs the case leaves to others (l.85-86); CANON A34 bars it as a trigger; the timing fact stays in the store.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; the 2027 rise (NT$1,400, +4.745%) is one boom year's jump, context for row 5.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; D1 equals the minimum in 2025 and 2026, evidence for row 14; all industries, not the arts.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; drop the unsourced the reverse of what most people assume; six years incl. 2021.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; median pay +1.43% after prices since 2020, so Baumol's wage drift was weak mid-scale; supports row 26's kill of claim 4.

Tue 17 Nov: store only: arts median 1.27 to 1.15 times the floor (2020-2025, read at source); the 2031-32 meeting is Keel's straight-line arithmetic and breaks before it meets (the card's own critique), so say may, never will.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; the arts-pay input series (1.88% a year 2015-2025, Table 19 read at source) behind rows 23 and 26.
Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (4) store: arts pay beat Taiwan prices by only about 0.4 points a year (CPI 1.49%, agrees with Q10-017's 1.47%); the evidence that kills claim 4.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; arts pay fell from 0.874 to 0.849 of all-industry pay (2016 to 2025); colour for Baumol's offsets, two sources spliced.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; fix the analogy: in 2021 the floor still rose 0.84%, so a fixed payment bought slightly less floor time, not never less; one pandemic year.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; 2026 part-year arts pay (+1.81% average, +1.01% median) is the slow path even in a boom.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; full employer cost about 24% above regular pay (604,258 / 12 / 40,634, checked), the basis of row 1's NT$50,355 staff-month.

Tue 17 Nov: store only; the Labour Insurance Act itself was not read, so check its start year (7.5% at the 2009 amendment, raised from the third year) and that 13% includes the 1% employment insurance before any use.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e store and questions: minimum-wage path 42.0 to 29.6 staff-months, 29.5% fewer (Keel arithmetic, checked: NT$39,008 and NT$55,330); straight-line past pace, never a forecast or a second printed figure.
Tue 17 Nov: 3e store and questions: arts-pay path 34.7 to 29.4 staff-months, 15.4% fewer (checked); slow end of the band.
Tue 17 Nov: 3e store: quote a band (about 29-42 staff-months per payment), never one figure; the paths cross by 2042, so the band is the honest form.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e questions: first-to-tenth loss 12.5% at prices to 30% at the floor (checked); the 23% twice-prices case is a sensitivity on Baumol and Bowen's old ratio, not a forecast; store, since claim 4 shows no second printed figure is needed.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (4): answers a judge's what about wages: a wage-heavy Taiwan blend keeps 67%-69% (77% at arts pay) against NUMBERS 8d's about 70%, so one figure suffices (blend checked); say it as Keel arithmetic at a steady exchange rate, from 2026 levels (16 years) against 8d's 15 from 1 Jan 2027, and never the verdict's 68.4% from end-2026.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; the primary Baumol (1967) quote, the APA source if a Baumol clause is ever used; H3-112 keeps Baumol as colour only.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; Baumol (1999): costs rise faster than prices and the only escapes are amateurs or fewer players; an orchestra is not a residency.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; the 2-to-1 ratio behind row 25's twice-prices case, via Heilbrun (2003); Baumol and Bowen (1966) not read.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; the predicted cost gap did not happen because organisations adapted; residency management, not the investment plan.

Tue 17 Nov: 3.0 store, beside H9-119: a fixed budget shrinks quietly (Broadway casts 15.8 to 8.1), never by a missed payment; never in Laura's text to co-sponsors as her residency shrinking; Broadway is commercial.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; Millay Colony staff 30.7%-38.3% of expenses; label the filing years at ProPublica before use (2023 figure secondary); the anchor for rows 33-34.
Tue 17 Nov: arithmetic on Q9c-017's Treasure Hill staff (NT$730,000 a head, NT$60,900 a month); carry that figure there as scale only, never as Laura's staffing cost.
Tue 17 Nov: same staff-share point as Q102-032; carry AFTA's 35% (FY2001, local arts agencies, read at source) there as a second check.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; wages +35% against non-personnel +3% (Washington arts nonprofits, 2019-2024): rising pay squeezes programmes first; one US state, post-pandemic.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; Taiwan's CPI rent index +1.38% a year 2015-2025, faster since 2021; 2014-2024 levels from a secondary site, open cpisplrent.xls before use.

Tue 17 Nov: store only; the rent index smooths new-lease steps; its weights (1.39% plus 13.85%) are the 2023 document's, not row 36's 147.82 per thousand, so name the base; a residency lease is beyond the plan's 3e limits.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; Taiwan services prices above 2% a year since 2022 against under 1.5% in 2018-2021.
Tue 17 Nov: arithmetic on Q9c-002's NT$800 daily allowance (2,048 resident-days per payment); carry it there as scale only; a grant floor, not a market price or a residency plan.

Tue 17 Nov: same principle as H7-088 (inflation decides what the payments buy, never whether they are paid; TNA's nonexistent inflation risk is about funding); carry the staff-month band from Q102-024 there as questions material only.

Tue 17 Nov: links Q49-036 and Q10d-018 with no new source; Q49-036 already says the ten payments do the job public capital cannot; add NCAF's salaried grants there; never that her money qualifies the residency for grants.
